name: undo_job
summary: Undo a finished place or remove job (place_cables, place_pipes, place_chutes, remove_*, place_structure, remove_structure; the last 16): remove what it built, build back what it removed. Dry run by default; confirm to undo.

help.text: The inverse, from a snapshot taken when the job started (position, turn, build state, label). Pieces come back through place_cables, place_pipes and place_chutes (the pieces form, one run per tool and grade; a long straight as singles), so every guard applies; everything else through place_structure. paste_blueprint has its own undo. Host only.
help.keys: job_id, tool, status, plan {remove, restore, diverged, notes, ready, ...}, remove_arguments, place_arguments, removal, placement, piece_runs [{tool, arguments, reply}], resolved_networks, gas_hold.

removal.text: A tool that builds pieces back removes its own pieces in its first piece run (remove_ids, no refund), in the same job, so a network is never left cut between jobs. Everything else is removed first by remove_structure (refund_to ground puts its refund where each piece stood). When the first run alone cannot rejoin the network, its dry run says would_split and the undo is refused. A burnt cable the job removed is never built again; plan.notes says so.

diverged.summary: When the world differs from what the job left.
diverged.text: Refused, status refused with plan.diverged naming why: something it built is gone or is another prefab; something it removed has no snapshot, stood off the grid's axes, or is a piece no coil or kit lays; the job had not finished; or an earlier undo of it ran (plan.undone_by lists those jobs: undo them, the last first, to have it back).

facts.summary: Undo a job past the last 16.
facts.text: The last 16 jobs to end, across every client, are kept with their final reply. For an older one pass the four lists its job_ended event (subscribe, topic jobs) or its final reply carries (created_ids, removed, placed and the swapped pieces): undo_job plans from them, and plan.notes says so. They count only while the job's snapshots are kept (the last 32 jobs); past that the job is job_not_found. While the job is among the 16 they are ignored and its own final reply is used.

runs.summary: The dry run and the real run.
runs.text: Dry run: status dry_run, plan {remove, restore, diverged, notes, ready}, remove_arguments, place_arguments, piece_runs [{tool, arguments, reply}], removal and placement dry runs; plan.ready only when every one is ready. A real run makes the same checks, then starts each job queued behind the one before (wait), each checked against the world the earlier ones leave; poll each with its own tool's job_id. Source: the job's own from_id (from_id overrides); removing what a free placement built gives nothing back. acknowledge_gas_lost passes to every call.

job_id.description: The job to undo (run-N, place-N, remove-N).

dry_run.description: Default true: report only, change nothing (see jobs).

items.description: A network id, {reference_id, port}, or a device id.

allow_bridge.description: Passed to every piece run: networks and devices whose joining is meant (see networks/bridging).

from_id.description: The source for every call; default the job's own, else the player.

refund_to.description: Where every removal's refund goes: a target list, or one word (see refunds).

created_ids.description: For a job past the last 16: every id it built, as its job_ended event gives them (topic facts).

items.description: An id, or a thing with its reference_id.

removed.description: For a job past the last 16: every id it removed, as its job_ended event gives them (topic facts).

old_reference_id.description: The piece the run took away.

new_reference_id.description: The piece it built in its place.

changed.description: For a job past the last 16: the pieces a run swapped, old for new, as its job_ended event gives them (topic facts).

placed.description: For a job past the last 16: the things it built with their prefab, as its job_ended event gives them (topic facts).
